indoor-air-pollutant.def: A pollutant in the air inside a building, such as radon, formaldehyde, carbon monoxide, asbestos fibers or smoke from indoor stoves. Tight, poorly ventilated buildings let them build up.

radon.def: A colorless, odorless radioactive gas formed when uranium in rock and soil decays. It seeps into buildings through foundation cracks and is a leading cause of lung cancer.

asbestos.def: A fibrous mineral once used in insulation, tiles and pipe wrap. When it is damaged, its fibers get into the air and can cause lung disease and cancer if breathed in.

formaldehyde.def: A VOC given off by pressed-wood furniture, cabinets, glues and some fabrics, especially when new. It irritates the eyes, nose and throat and can cause cancer.

sick-building.def: Sick building syndrome: headaches, eye irritation, coughing and tiredness that people feel in a particular building and that ease when they leave, usually from VOCs and poor ventilation.
